texts.preamble: Delhi Administration vs B.B Garg Etc on 3 February, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Abhishek Kumar Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi District: New Delhi Cr Cases 39092/2016 Delhi Administration Vs. B.B Garg Etc. Judgment
texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 3. The accused namely Ram Swaroop had challenged the order before the appellate court. Page No. 2 of 11 conviction for defect in the product, even at the stage of packaging, before it left the factory premises. 4. Accordingly, arguments were heard afresh at length on behalf of the accused Ram Swaroop and the department. Furthermore, none of the parties requested or filed any application for adducing any additional evidence. 5. During the course of arguments, the accused did not dispute the proceedings conducted by the department regarding the lifting of the sample or the report of the food analyst finding the milk sample not conforming to the standards prescribed under the PFA Act and rules. The accused Ram Swaroop had argued primarily with respect to his role in the commission of the crime. He had stated that he could not have made liable on account of the nomination in his favour, which extended to the distribution activities whereas the sample was lifted from a different unit in the establishment, where the accused had no role to play. Thus, filing of the complaint against him was not proper on account of the limited nomination. Thus, the quality control of the milk and its processing was not within the domain of his area of operation which extended to distribution. Accordingly, accused prayed that he is liable to be acquitted in the present case. Page No. 3 of 11 conduct of the business and for not preventing the commission Delhi Administration vs B.B Garg Etc on 3 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9796682/ 2 of the offence under the PFA act. Further, area of operation would not make any difference with respect to the liability of the accused. 8. It is the case of the complainant that on 06.08.2003 at about 10.00 am, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh. R.K. Bhaskar purchased a sample of 'Pasteurized Full Cream Milk' a food article for analysis from the convict B.B. Garg acting for convict M/s. Delhi Milk Scheme, Shadi Pur, West Patel Nagar, New Delhi-8, where the said food article was stored for sale and convict B.B. Garg was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. 9. Further, the sample consisted 3 x 500ml sealed polythene packets 'Pasteurized Full Cream Milk', having identical label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. S.K. Nanda, LHA, after proper homogenization i.e by cutting the polythene packets and pouring the contents in a clean and dry patila and re-pouring the milk with the help of other clean and dry Patila. 10. Then, the Food Inspector divided the sample into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles. Further, 40 drops of formalin were added in each sample bottle. Digitally Eachsignedsample ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Page No. 4 of 11 bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to convict B.B.Garg and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 06.08.2003. Thereafter, a panchnama was also prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by Fl were signed by convict B.B. Garg and the other witness Sh. S.K. Nanda, LHA. It was also averred in the complaint that before starting sample proceeding, efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh.S.K. Nanda, LHA was joined as witness. 11. It is further stated in the complaint that one counter part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 03/LHA/5404 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII underseal cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst (herein after referred to as PA), Delhi and two counter parts of the sample along with two copies of memos in Form VII were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition. 12. Accordingly, Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be non-conforming to the standards prescribed under PFA Act and Rules by stating that the milk fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 6.0% and moreover, there was no indication of best before on the poly packets. It is further the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 B.B.Garg was the vendor-cum-nominee of M/s Delhi Milk Scheme, Shadi Pur, West Patel, Nagar New Delhi at the time of sampling. There are four more nominees under PFA Act besides convict No. 1 B.B. Garg who are vendor-cum-nominees i.e convict No. 2 Ashok Bansal, convict No. 3 Vinay Bagga, accused No. 4 Ram Swroop and convict No. 5 J.S. Rathore and all the five abovementioned nominees were incharge and responsible for day today conduct of the business of the said Delhi Milk Scheme. 14. Thereafter, on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 03.03.2004 alleging violation of section 2(ia) (a) (m) and 2(ix) (k) of PFA Act, 1954read with Rule 32 (i) of PFA Rules 1955, which is punishable U/s.16(1) (a) of the PFA Act read with section 7 of the PFA Act. 15. It is important to note that an application was moved on behalf of convict B.B.Garg and on the basis of the same, another counterpart sample U/s. 13 (2) was sent to Director, CFL for analysis, who vide report dated 26.04.2004, opined that the sample article of 'Pasteurized Full Cream Milk' does not conform to the standard of full cream milk as perPFA, 1954 as the same milk fat was less than the prescribed limit of 6% and it was shown the value 4.8%. During the course of the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses, who reiterated the contents of the complaint, proved the documents and the sample reports. All the witnesses were duly cross examined. Thereafter, prosecution evidence was closed. 17. The statement of the accused persons was recorded on 10.02.2010.

Offences by companies. -- (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company-- (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereinafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2024.02.03 17:03:09 +0530 Cr. Page No. 8 of 11 of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. (2) Any company may, by order in writing, authorise any of its directors or managers (such manager being employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity) to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the commission by the company or any offence under this Act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority, in such form and in such manner as may be Delhi Administration vs B.B Garg Etc on 3 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9796682/ 5 prescribed, that it has nominated such director or manager as the person responsible, along with the written consent of such director or manager for being so nominated. Explanation.--Where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, different persons may be nominated under this sub-section in relation to different establishments or branches or units and the person nominated in relation to any establishment, branch or unit shall be deemed to be the person responsible in respect of such establishment, branch or unit. (3) The person nominated under sub-section (2) shall, until-- (i) further notice cancelling such nomination is received from the company by the Local (Health) Authority; or (ii) he ceases to be a director or, as the case may be, manager of the company; or (iii) he makes a request in writing to the Local (Health) Authority, under intimation to the company, to cancel the nomination [which request shall be complied with by the Local (Health) Authority.] whichever is the earliest, continue to be the person responsible: Provided that where such person ceases to be a director or, as the case may be, manager of the company, he shall intimate the fact of such cesser to the Local (Health) Authority: Provided further that where such person makes a request under clause (iii), the Local (Health) Authority shall not cancel such nomination with effect from a date earlier than the date on which the request is made. Page No. 9 of 11 (4) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing sub- sections, where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to, any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary, or other officer of the company, [not being a person nominated under sub-section (2) such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
